question.explanation:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\dfrac00,$ as follows:

\[ \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \dfrac{x-y}{\sqrt{x}-\sqrt y} = \dfrac{4-4}{\sqrt{4}-\sqrt 4} = \dfrac{0}{0} \]

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

\begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \dfrac{x-y}{\sqrt{x}-\sqrt y} &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \dfrac{(x-y) \big( \sqrt{x}+\sqrt y \big)}{\big( \sqrt x - \sqrt y \big) \big( \sqrt{x}+\sqrt y \big)} \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \dfrac{(x-y) \big( \sqrt{x}+\sqrt y \big)}{\big(\sqrt{x}\big)^2-\big(\sqrt{y}\big)^2} \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \dfrac{(x-y) \big( \sqrt{x}+\sqrt y \big)}{x-y} \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \left(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt y\right) \end{align*}

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

\begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (4,4)}} \left(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt y\right) &= \sqrt{4}+\sqrt{4} \\[5pt] &=2+2 \\[5pt] &= 4 \end{align*}

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $4.$

example.title: Calculating Limits of Multivariable Functions Using Conjugate Multiplication

question.explanation:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\dfrac00,$ as follows:

\[ \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}- y}{x-y^2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1}- 1}{1-1^2} = \dfrac{0}{0} \]

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the numerator:

\begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}- y}{x-y^2} &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}}\dfrac{(\sqrt{x}- y) \big( \sqrt{x}+ y \big)}{\big(x-y^2 \big) \big( \sqrt{x}+ y \big)} \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{ \big(\sqrt{x} \big)^2- y^2 } {\big(x-y^2 \big) \big( \sqrt{x}+y \big)} \\[5pt] &=\displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{ x- y^2}{\big(x-y^2 \big) \big( \sqrt{x}+y \big)} \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{ 1}{\sqrt{x}+ y } \end{align*}

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

\begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (1,1)}} \dfrac{ 1}{\sqrt{x}+ y } &= \dfrac{ 1}{\sqrt{1}+ 1 } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 1}{1+1 }\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $ \dfrac{1}{2}.$

example.title: Calculating Limits of Multivariable Functions Using Conjugate Multiplication

question.explanation:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0},$ as follows: \begin{align} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{xz + yz}{x^2 - y^2} & = \dfrac{(-1)(2) + 1(2)}{(-1)^2 - 1^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{-2 + 2}{1 - 1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{0} \end{align}

However, we can simplify the limit by canceling common factors in the numerator and denominator: \begin{align} \require{cancel} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{xz + yz}{x^2 - y^2} & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{z(x + y)}{(x + y)(x - y)} \\[5pt] & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{z\cancel{(x + y)}}{\cancel{(x + y)}(x - y)}\\[5pt] & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{z}{x - y} \end{align}

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it using direct substitution: \begin{align} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (-1,1,2)} \dfrac{z}{x - y} & = \dfrac{2}{-1 - 1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{(-2)}\\[5pt] & = -1 \end{align}

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $-1.$

example.title: Calculating Limits of Multivariable Rational Functions by Factoring

question.explanation:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0},$ as follows: \begin{align} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} \dfrac{x^3 - 3x^2 y + 3xy^2 - y^3}{x^2 - 2xy + y^2} & = \dfrac{2^3 - 3(2^2)(2) + 3(2)(2^2) - 2^3}{2^2 - 2(2)(2) + 2^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{8 - 24 + 24 - 8}{4 - 8 + 4}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{0} \end{align}

However, we can simplify the limit by canceling common factors in the numerator and denominator: \begin{align} \require{cancel} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} \dfrac{x^3 - 3x^2 y + 3xy^2 - y^3}{x^2 - 2xy + y^2} & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} \dfrac{(x - y)^3}{(x - y)^2} \\[5pt] & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} \dfrac{(x-y)(x - y)^2}{(x - y)^2}\\[5pt] & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} \dfrac{(x-y)\cancel{(x - y)^2}}{\cancel{(x - y)^2}}\\[5pt] & = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} (x - y) \end{align}

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it using direct substitution: \begin{align} \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (2,2)} (x - y) & = 2 - 2 = 0 \end{align}

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $0.$

example.title: Calculating Limits of Multivariable Rational Functions by Factoring

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the limit given below? \[ \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to (0,0)} \, \dfrac{2xy}{3y^2 - x^2} \]

  1. The limit evaluates to $0$ along the path $y = 0$
  2. The limit evaluates to $\dfrac 2 3$ along the path $y = x$
  3. The limit does not exist
question.explanation:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0}\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \lim\limits_{\mathbf{x}\to (0,0)} \, \dfrac{2xy}{3y^2 - x^2} & = \dfrac{2(0)(0)}{3(0^2) - 0^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{0 - 0}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{0} \end{align}

However, the function cannot be simplified by canceling common factors in the numerator and denominator:

We attempt to evaluate the limit by approaching $(0,0)$ from different paths.

  • Statement I is true. Taking $\mathbf{x} \to (0,0)$ along the path $y = 0,$ we have \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{\mathbf{x} \to (0,0) \\ \:\: y=0} \, \dfrac{2xy}{3y^2 - x^2} & = \lim_{x \to 0} \, \dfrac{2x(0)}{3(0^2) - x^2} \\[5pt] & = \lim_{x\to 0} 0 \\[5pt] &= 0 . \end{align*}

  • Statement II is false. Taking $\mathbf{x} \to (0,0)$ along the path $y=x,$ we have \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{\mathbf{x} \to (0,0) \\ \:\: y=x}\, \dfrac{2xy}{3y^2 - x^2} & = \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2x(x)}{3x^2 - x^2} \\[5pt] & = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2x^2}{2x^2} \\[5pt] & = \lim_{x \to 0} 1 \\[5pt] & = 1 \end{align*}

  • Statement III is true. Because the limit evaluates to different results on two different paths, we conclude that the limit does not exist: \[ \lim\limits_{\mathbf{x}\to (0,0)} \, \dfrac{2xy}{3y^2 - x^2} = \text{DNE} \]
